mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays below baseline while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, weekday destination traffic will stay suppressed and retail-and-recreation mobility will decline further over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both move toward baseline for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in GROCERY_PHARM signals more local errand substitution and less discretionary shopping, which pulls RETAIL_REC downward over the next one to two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 to 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility remains more than 50 points above baseline, leisure time is reallocated outdoors rather than to shopping districts, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds +50 and stays above that level for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to its prior four-week mean after PARKS stays above +50 for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains around 25 to 30 points below baseline while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, the city is still operating under movement restraint, which should keep retail-and-recreation mobility subdued for the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -20 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +2
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises toward baseline while TRANSIT remains below -20 and RESIDENTIAL remains above +2.

mechanism_narrative: In winter-like conditions, sustained PARKS surges are a sign of outdoor leisure substitution and reduced mall and restaurant visitation, so RETAIL_REC should weaken over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:weekly PARKS is far above its baseline while RETAIL_REC remains negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases for four straight weeks despite PARKS staying clearly above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES drops further and TRANSIT fails to recover, commuter-linked discretionary purchases will not materialize, so retail-and-recreation mobility should remain below its recent average over the next week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls week-on-week while TRANSIT stays below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the following week despite a simultaneous weekly drop in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining below -25.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT toward baseline precedes more shopping trips because accessibility improves before retail visits do, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points from the prior week and remains above -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the next 14 days after TRANSIT improves by at least 3 points and remains above -25.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL indicates precautionary staying-home behavior that crowds out discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC should decline over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both stay above baseline for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-four-week mean even though GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both remain above baseline for two weeks.
